name: Alberta
summary_text: Alberta is the only jurisdiction in the country to pass laws targeting transgender people as a class and then shield those laws from judicial review. Three bills, announced in January 2024 and enacted in December 2024: the Education Amendment Act 2024 requires parental notification/consent before staff use a student's gender-related preferred name or pronouns (in full force since 1 September 2025); the Health Statutes Amendment Act 2024 prohibits puberty blockers and hormone therapy for minors; and a vital-statistics rule was amended. A 2025 government bill invoked the constitutional notwithstanding clause over all three laws, and after it passed, a Court of King's Bench judge lifted the injunction that had been pausing the care ban; a government appeal succeeded, removing the injunction. Two national 2SLGBTQ+ organisations, with five gender-diverse youth, continue a constitutional challenge despite the shield ("the fight isn't over"). These school and healthcare provisions are primarily resident-facing and carry small traveler-facing weight. The more directly relevant signal is the documented street-level pattern in Calgary: from 2023 a pastor led repeated disruptions of library drag-storytime events — charging into a library classroom and shouting homophobic and transphobic slurs at parents and children, who left crying — and the litigation has run for years: a conviction for harassing a librarian was upheld on appeal, acquittals on disturbance and mischief charges were overturned with a new trial ordered, and a further breach conviction followed in 2026. Reporting from March 2023 noted many drag events cancelled or postponed in Calgary as threats and protests escalated. The pairing of trans-targeting legislation, a judicial-override shield and a documented event-cancellation pattern marks a clear hardening of provincial posture.

sources.title: Alberta legislation on transgender youth, student pronouns and sex education set to become law | CBC News
sources.claim_summary: National public broadcaster (4 December 2024): the trio of Alberta bills affecting transgender people — pronoun/parental-notification opt-ins in schools, the ban on gender-affirming care for minors, and a vital-statistics change — passed the legislature's final stage; 2SLGBTQ+ advocacy groups say they will continue legal action.

sources.title: Bill 9 not discouraging 2SLGBTQ+ groups challenging Alberta laws affecting transgender youth | CBC News
sources.claim_summary: National public broadcaster (December 2025): Bill 9 invoked the notwithstanding clause to shield the three transgender-affecting laws from legal action; Egale Canada and Skipping Stone, with five gender-diverse youth, say they will continue the court challenge of the care-ban law regardless ("the fight isn't over").

sources.title: 'Your call for action turned on you,' says judge in rejecting appeal of convicted pastor | CBC News
sources.claim_summary: National public broadcaster: appellate court upholds pastor Derek Reimer's conviction for harassing a librarian during his disruptions of Calgary library drag-storytime events ("your call for action turned on you"), part of years of litigation over the protest pattern.

sources.title: Acquittals overturned, new trial ordered for preacher who led anti-drag protest | CBC News
sources.claim_summary: National public broadcaster: Reimer's acquittals on disturbing-the-peace and mischief charges over a library drag-reading protest are overturned on appeal and new trials are ordered, extending the Calgary drag-event court saga.

sources.title: Calgary pastor faces multiple charges after disrupting drag storytime | Xtra Magazine
sources.claim_summary: LGBT magazine (March 2023): within "a rising tide of anti-LGBTQ2S+ and anti-drag protests in Calgary", pastor Derek Reimer was charged after aggressively entering a Seton library classroom and shouting homophobic and transphobic slurs at parents and children at a drag storytime event; police describe several people scaring children and refusing to leave, and note many drag events cancelled or postponed citywide as threats escalated.
